title: Text overlapping in transfer notification in RTL
line: In right-to-left languages the Speed and Average Speed readings under a file transfer's speed chart no longer draw on top of each other.
explanation: LegendLayout sizes each legend item by clamping the column width between the item's LegendLayout.minimumWidth and maximumWidth, but an unset maximumWidth reads as 0. The notification's 'Average Speed' row doesn't set one, so it got width 0 and its labels overflowed its cell; in LTR that overflow goes right and looks fine, but in RTL the mirrored RowLayout puts it to the left, on top of the 'Speed' item. The change only applies the maximum width when the item actually sets one, keeping the minimum width as the lower bound.

commits.message:
controls/LegendLayout: don't shrink items without a maximum width to zero

An item that doesn't set LegendLayout.maximumWidth was clamped to the
unset value of 0, so its content overflowed its cell. In right-to-left
layouts it overflowed to the left over the previous item; now it isn't.

BUG: 516577

media.caption: plasmashell -reverse, fake copy job, Details open: the two speed legends under the chart are drawn over each other.
Same steps with the fix: 'Speed' and 'Average Speed' each sit in their own cell and are readable.
Legend row zoomed: both readings readable.

review.text: Correct root-cause fix in KQuickCharts: LegendLayout::updatePolish() unconditionally passed attached->maximumWidth() (which defaults to 0 when unset) to std::clamp(), collapsing items without a maximum width to 0 px (and risking UB when minimumWidth > 0), which caused RTL delegates to overflow left over the previous item. Checking isMaximumWidthValid() and applying std::min then std::max matches determineColumns() cleanly and fixes the overlap with all 8 kquickcharts autotests passing. Before/after RTL screenshots confirm both speed readings sit cleanly side by side.
